proposal.root_cause: Billing import validation rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, unit_scaling: none) compares raw AMI register values directly to 12-month m3 consumption history, but v4.2 meters (rollout 2026-06) report registers in '0.1 m3' units — a 10x mismatch that misclassifies valid high-consumption-looking-but-normal reads as outliers, causing rejection at import and forced estimate substitution (E-11, E-12, E-13). This confirmed mechanism explains 1,184 of 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills; its reach into the 1,785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (E-03) is unconfirmed (U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM, CRITICAL, OPEN).
proposal.why_agent_needed: Once SR-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM-QUERY and SR-DETERMINISTIC-DISPUTE-TRIAGE are run, most dispute tickets fall into deterministic, field-matchable categories (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION vs NO_READ_RECEIVED vs a possible third pattern); an agent would only add value for the residual, genuinely unclassified exception tickets that don't match any known pattern, to draft case-specific explanations for Billing Ops review (never to write bills, per K-BILLWRITE).

proposal.summary: The initial request (SH-CS, CL-01) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and auto-fix "whatever is causing wrong bills" after dispute volume roughly doubled (E-07). Investigation first framed the problem as route-completion/field-staffing plus billing-import mishandling (PD-1@v1), but that premise was invalidated once E-11 showed only 56 of 1,240 "ESTIMATED" disputed bills truly lacked a read — 1,184 had a valid AMI read wrongly rejected at import. The successor problem (PD-1@v2) is that billing-config rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit conversion (E-12), misreads v4.2 AMI meters reporting in 0.1 m3 (E-13) as high-consumption outliers, forcing estimate substitution and explaining the surge (E-11, confirmed independently by E-14, E-15, E-16). The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, confined to the narrow verified scope (verify_meter_firmware_unit_scaling on DA-MDMS, per SD-2), because the DEFINE Gate only reached CONDITIONAL_PASS and three verification obligations about the broader scope remain open.
key_points: Root-cause mechanism is confirmed: BV-17's missing unit conversion (unit_scaling: none, E-12) misclassifies normal v4.2-meter consumption (0.1 m3 vs m3, E-13) as high-consumption, causing valid AMI reads to be rejected at import and estimate-substituted (E-11), independently reproduced by E-14, E-15, E-16.

Competing explanations were tested and rejected: field-reader shortage/route-completion gap (H-FIELD-READ-GAP, contradicted by E-11 despite E-01/E-05/E-09), AMI export gap (H-AMI-EXPORT-GAP), ticket response-speed framing (H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING, contradicted by E-01/E-02), and estimate-logic flaw (H-ESTIMATE-LOGIC-FLAW, contradicted by E-12/E-13).
Tariff change was ruled out as a cause (CL-02/E-04 corroborated authoritatively by E-06, zero tariff-change records this year).

The release does not fulfill the original request to auto-fix bills: no automated bill writes are permitted (K-BILLWRITE), and the structural remedy for BV-17 (SR-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-FIX) requires ORG-UTIL's own change-management process on a tool surface that is read-only for billing-config.

Released scope is limited to one verified item, verify_meter_firmware_unit_scaling:DA-MDMS (SD-2 release_scope); analyze_disputed_bills_by_cause, monitor_dispute_volume_trend, and recommend_billing_rule_correction stay excluded pending open obligations.

A semantic inconsistency is flagged in the release's own limitation text: it states DA-BILL, DA-MDMS and DA-RULES completeness is UNKNOWN, but the data_assets record shows DA-BILL and DA-MDMS as COMPLETE (only DA-RULES is UNKNOWN).
limitations_explained: The DEFINE Gate for this problem reached only CONDITIONAL_PASS, with deferred items tracked as open verification obligations (VOBs) rather than fully resolved before release.

Three VOBs remain OPEN and keep the broader scope out of this release: whether the BV-17 mechanism also explains the 1,785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM), whether ticket volume alone is a valid success metric (VOB-U-METRIC-VALIDITY), and whether the BV-17 fix is feasible in time (VOB-U-RULE-FIX-FEASIBILITY).

The actual fix to BV-17 cannot be executed within this engagement: the billing-config tool is read-only, and no change-management SLA fits the stated remaining time window, so the one remedy that removes the root cause (SR-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-FIX) is left for ORG-UTIL's own process.
A falling dispute-ticket count is not by itself proof that bills became more accurate; it must be corroborated against the rejection-share metric before declaring success.
Even with deterministic triage of known-pattern bills, a residual unclassified category among ACTUAL-read disputed bills still needs case-by-case human handling.
DA-RULES' completeness status is recorded as UNKNOWN in data_assets, leaving residual data-quality risk even for the narrow scope that was released.

The release's own limitation text contains a self-reported inconsistency: it claims DA-BILL/DA-MDMS/DA-RULES completeness is all UNKNOWN, but the authoritative data_assets record marks DA-BILL and DA-MDMS COMPLETE.
